Inspected the current draft definition body: “Let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper, closed and convex, and let $t>0$. For $v\in\mathbb R^n$, define the set-valued proximal mapping
$$\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v)=\left\{u\in\mathbb R^n:g(u)+\frac{\|u-v\|_2^2}{2t}\le g(w)+\frac{\|w-v\|_2^2}{2t}\text{ for every }w\in\mathbb R^n\right\}.$$
The existence and uniqueness theorem on this page proves that this set is a singleton for every admissible $g,t,v$; its unique member is also denoted $\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v)$.” Consumer interface: declared direct dependency; used in the carrier proof or definition Current body text is authoring-interface evidence only and does not certify supplier acceptance.

Inspected the current draft definition body: “Let $F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be a proper convex extended-real function ([[def-extended-reals]]). For $\mu>0$, say that $F$ is **$\mu$-strongly convex** if for every $x,y\in\operatorname{dom}F$ and $0<\theta<1$,
$$F((1-\theta)x+\theta y)\le(1-\theta)F(x)+\theta F(y)-\frac\mu2\theta(1-\theta)\|x-y\|_2^2.$$
This definition permits $F$ to be extended-real-valued outside its effective domain. The endpoint cases are identities and are not included in the strict range for $\theta$.” Consumer interface: F4 in steps 2.1: [F4] [[def-strong-convex-composite-objective]]: $\mu$-strong convexity is the strong-Jensen inequality with decrement $(\mu/2)\theta(1-\theta)|x-y|^2$. Current body text is authoring-interface evidence only and does not certify supplier acceptance.

Inspected the current draft definition body: “Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$. Its effective domain is $\operatorname{dom}g=\{x:g(x)<+\infty\}$. The function is **proper** if $\operatorname{dom}g\ne\varnothing$; it is **convex** if
$$g((1-\theta)x+\theta y)\le(1-\theta)g(x)+\theta g(y)\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb R^n,\ 0\le\theta\le1),$$
using the endpoint convention $0\cdot(+\infty)=0$ of [[def-convex-and-strictly-convex-functionals-on-a-banach-space]]. It is **closed** (equivalently, lower semicontinuous in the extended-real convex-analysis convention used here) if its epigraph
$$\operatorname{epi}g=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R:g(x)\le s\}$$
is closed in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$. The proximal-gradient items on this page assume $g$ is proper, closed and convex.” Consumer interface: F5 in steps 1.1: [F5] [[def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn]]: proper means nonempty effective domain, convexity is the extended-real convexity inequality, and closedness means closed epigraph. Current body text is authoring-interface evidence only and does not certify supplier acceptance.

Inspected the current draft statement body: “Let $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper, closed and convex in the epigraph convention of [[def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn]]. For every $t>0$ and $v\in\mathbb R^n$, the set $\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v)$ is a singleton. Its unique element $u$ satisfies the resolvent equivalence
$$u=\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (v-u)/t\in\partial g(u).$$
For any $v_1,v_2$ and $u_i=\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(v_i)$,
$$\|u_1-u_2\|_2^2\le\langle u_1-u_2,v_1-v_2\rangle.$$
In particular the proximal map is nonexpansive.” Consumer interface: F7 in steps 3.1: [F7] [[thm-proximal-operator-existence-resolvent-firm-nonexpansive]]: for every proper closed convex g, prox_g(v) is a singleton. Current body text is authoring-interface evidence only and does not certify supplier acceptance.
